note: What the harness redacts as a secret, in every text it writes down: its log lines, what it files into memory, and the text files a tool saves in its capture folder. Two halves: the agent's own configured secrets, matched by value, and the shapes below, matched wherever they appear. A key that is neither one of the agent's configured secrets nor one of these shapes is caught by neither.

markers.note: What stands where a secret stood. `redacted_value` replaces the value of a credential-named assignment, the name kept (`GH_TOKEN='<a redacted value>'`), and is the router's marker byte for byte; `redacted` replaces everything else.

configured_values.note: The agent's own secrets, matched by value wherever they appear: the value of every environment variable whose whole name names a credential by `credential_assignment` (its `words` and `tail`, nothing before the word but capitals, digits and `_`), and of every credential the harness holds under such a name. A value shorter than `minimum_length` is not blanked by a bare match, so an ordinary word is never taken out of a memory; it is still blanked where a credential name introduces it, by `credential_assignment`. Twenty is the floor the vendor-key rules use.

vendor_keys.note: A key is the prefix, then a run of at least `minimum_run` characters of `run`. Both are regular-expression fragments in the syntax Python's re, RE2 and VRL share (no lookaround). Order matters: a reader tries the rules in this order, so `sk-or-` is tried before `sk-`. A prefixed match glued to a letter or digit before it whose run holds no digit and no capital is a word (`task-specification`), not a key.

rules.vendors: OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, xAI, and BaseCradle's three-letter kinds

credential_assignment.note: An assignment whose name names a credential: capitals, digits and `_`, then one of `words`, then optionally `tail`, then `=`. The value after the `=`, past any gap (a run of whitespace and C0 and C1 control characters) after it, is redacted whatever it looks like, and the name stays. This is the fleet log canary's `credential_assignment` rule, `[A-Z0-9_]*(KEY|TOKEN|SECRET|PASSWORD|PASSPHRASE)(_BASE)?=[^ ",}]{8,}`, which reads a value as a run of anything but `value_stops`, at least `value_minimum_length` long.

bearer.note: An authorization header: the scheme word in any case, a gap (whitespace or control characters), then a token of at least `minimum_token` characters of `token`. The scheme word and its token both go.

query_parameters.note: A key in a URL: `?` or `&`, one of `names` in any case, `=`, then the value, up to the next `&` or whitespace.

api_key_assignment.note: One of `names` in any case, then `=`, anywhere: the value up to the next `&`, `"` or whitespace.

headers.note: A header carrying a key of no stated shape: one of `names` in any case, then `:` or `=>` (or, after a quote, `:`, `=`, `=>` or `,`), then the value, up to the next whitespace, quote, backslash or `&`.

json_members.note: A JSON member whose name is exactly one of `names`, in any case, and whose value is a string: the string's contents go, its name and quotes stay.

heartbeat_url.note: A Better Stack heartbeat URL, whose secret is its path: from the URL's scheme when it has one, else from `path`, to the end of the run of non-whitespace.
